entities.summary: Guido Pisano was a prelate and diplomat from Pisa who played a crucial role in the papal court during the 12th century. He was promoted to the College of Cardinals and appointed to the deaconry of Santi Cosma e Damiano by Pope Innocent II on 4 March 1132. This appointment marked a significant turning point in his career, as it elevated him to a position of considerable influence within the Catholic Church. Pisano's connections to the papal court and his family's ties to the counts of Caprona made him a valuable asset to the Church, and his appointment demonstrates the complex web of alliances and power struggles that characterized the medieval papacy. As a result of his appointment, Pisano became embroiled in the intricate politics of the Church, navigating the treacherous waters of papal intrigue and rivalries between different factions. Despite the challenges he faced, Pisano's appointment also opened up new opportunities for him, including the chance to participate in high-level diplomatic missions and to shape the Church's policies on matters of great importance. Ultimately, Pisano's career was marked by a series of promotions and appointments that reflect his growing influence within the Church, and his legacy as a prelate and diplomat continues to be felt to this day.
